title: Chocolate Pecan Slab Pie Feeds More People and Disappears Faster
text:
1 days ago Chocolate Pecan Slab Pie combines the gooey center of Southern pecan pie with enough semisweet chocolate to satisfy brownie lovers. A buttery homemade crust lines a rectangular pan, making room for a filling of chocolate chips, corn syrup, brown sugar, eggs, vanilla, melted butter, and a generous amount of chopped pecans. As it bakes, the filling sets around the toasted nuts while remaining soft and sticky underneath. The shallow slab format creates more crisp edges than a traditional round pie and allows the dessert to be cut into neat squares that are easy to place on a party tray.
Photo by SURVIVEHACK.COM This is a practical centerpiece for Thanksgiving, Christmas, potlucks, bake sales, or any gathering where one eight-slice pie will not survive. Maple syrup or honey can replace the corn syrup for a different flavor, while dark chocolate produces a more intense, less-sweet result. Let the slab cool completely before slicing so the filling has time to firm. Small pieces are usually sufficient because every square is remarkably rich, although guests frequently ignore that advice. Serve them plain, dusted with powdered sugar, or warmed with vanilla ice cream. The dessert is familiar enough to please traditional pecan-pie fans but chocolatey enough to win over anyone who normally walks past the pie table.
